capitals.name: Velika Kladuša
capitals.note: Infobox capital; the republic was declared in Velika Kladuša on 27 September 1993.

rulers.name: Fikret Abdić
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Elected by the 400-member Constituent Assembly of 27 September 1993; the government was led by Zlatko Jušić; Abdić fled to Croatia after August 1995.

correction.text: Velika Kladuša and its surroundings, the part of the Bihać pocket held by Fikret Abdić; total area 420 km2 (infobox), 52,908 people (1991)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. A 12 km circle at Velika Kladuša (about 450 km2) stands for the infobox's 420 km2; the page names the municipalities of Bihać, Cazin and Velika Kladuša as the region, which would be larger, but gives no map. The enclave was defeated in 1994 and re-established the same year; the yearly shape is the same.

region.text: Velika Kladuša and the Bihać pocket's north-west

ledger.note: 27 September 1993: Fikret Abdić declares the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia. 'On 27 September 1993, Abdić declared the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia in Velika Kladuša'; a 400-member Constituent Assembly met the same day and elected him president. He made non-aggression pacts with Boban, Karadžić and the Krajina Serbs and met their prime ministers on 7 November 1993.

region.text: Velika Kladuša and the Bihać pocket

ledger.note: June 1994: the Bosnian army moves against the province. Bosnian government forces defeated the APZB 'during Operation Tiger in June and August 1994'; the page gives no day.
1994: Operation Tiger overruns the province. 'Bosnian government forces defeated the APZB during Operation Tiger in June and August 1994.'

Later in 1994: Operation Spider re-establishes the province. Abdić's forces 'were expelled later that year with the significant help of the Serbs in Operation Spider, after which the APZB was re-established'; the page gives no month.
26 July 1995: the province declares itself the independent Republic of Western Bosnia. 'The province declared itself the independent Republic of Western Bosnia on 26 July 1995.'

7 August 1995: the Republic of Western Bosnia is wiped out. 'The RZB was wiped out completely during the joint Croatian-Bosnian government army action on 7 August 1995'; Operation Storm had made it the last line of defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

region.text: the enclave around Velika Kladuša, to the Bosnian government

ledger.note: 7 August 1995: the end of Western Bosnia. Abdić fled to Croatia after the operation.

wars.name: Operation Tiger and Operation Spider (Bihać pocket, 1994)
wars.outcome: Operation Tiger (June and August 1994) defeated the province; Operation Spider, with Serb help, re-established it later in 1994; the joint Croatian-Bosnian army action of 7 August 1995 ended it.
wars.note: The Bosnian War page lists 'Western Bosnia' as a belligerent in 1994-95 but says nothing of Abdić or the province.

certainty.note: A besieged enclave inside the Bihać pocket; the page gives an area but no boundary.

sources.title: Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia
sources.note: Whole dossier: 27 September 1993, 420 km2, Operations Tiger and Spider, 26 July 1995, 7 August 1995.

notes: Requested as a counterpart by eu-22-e (named in notes only there). One page opened (the budget for a state with no Cliopatria shape is 1-2 pages). Not settled: the months of Operations Tiger and Spider (the page gives 'June and August 1994' and 'later that year'), the municipalities actually held, and the Bihać pocket around the enclave (held by the Bosnian army, 5th Corps). Gazetteer: Velika Kladuša is not in places (a 12 km circle is used).
